Google Cloud Content & Editorial

Want to know the latest from Google Cloud? Find it here in one handy location. Check back regularly for our newest updates, announcements, resources, events, learning opportunities, and more.

Tip: Not sure where to find what you’re looking for on the Google Cloud blog? Start here: Google Cloud blog 101: Full list of topics, links, and resources.

Nov 2 - Nov 6

  • Security for AI workloads with Model Armor

    Securing generative AI applications requires robust runtime protection against prompt injection and malicious inputs. Join Nicola Cardace on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 5:00 PM CET for a Community TechTalk exploring how to safeguard enterprise AI workloads using Model Armor. Discover practical patterns for implementing active model defense across your LLM endpoints.

    Register for the November 19 Community TechTalk

  • A5X accelerated by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 is now Generally Available

    Get the most out of A5X instances with Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer. Bringing together compute, storage, networking, and software co-designed as a single system. 

    Read more

Oct 26 - Oct 30

  • Simplify PostgreSQL Monitoring with the New AlloyDB Omni Web UI

    The newly released AlloyDB Omni Web UI delivers a centralized, graphical dashboard that simplifies the management of self-managed PostgreSQL workloads across hybrid, multi-cloud, and air-gapped environments. This browser-based console provides database administrators with deep, real-time insights into cluster health, hardware utilization, and active database connections. It also features built-in query diagnostics and performance tracking for AlloyDB’s columnar engine, enabling quick troubleshooting of bottlenecks without manual terminal commands. To learn more about setting up this monitoring interface, read the fullAlloyDB Omni Web UI Blog Post.
  • Leveraging "Antigravity" to architect high performance semantic model routers in Apigee

    Semantic model routing replaces rigid static paths with a lightweight helper model to dynamically classify and dispatch intent-driven LLM traffic. Join Saravanakumar Rajagopal on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 5:00 PM CET for a Community TechTalk exploring how to leverage Antigravity and skills to architect these intelligent multi-provider routing patterns natively inside Apigee. Discover how to optimize your AI infrastructure and enhance flexibility at scale.

    Register for the November 12 Community TechTalk

Oct 19 - Oct 23

  • From prompt to production: End-to-end AI workflows in Apigee

    Deploying an enterprise AI gateway does not require deep API or machine learning expertise. Using declarative workflows in Apigee, teams can spin up a fully governed LLM gateway in minutes using a few environment variables. Join Luis Cuellar on Thursday, October 29, 2026 for a Community TechTalk exploring end-to-end AI workflows. Discover how to layer essential defenses—including Model Armor for prompt protection, Cloud Data Loss Prevention (Cloud DLP) for sensitive data redaction, rate limiting, and response caching—before routing autonomous agent interactions through your gateway filters.

    Register for the October 29 Community TechTalk
  • Zero Standing Privileges with PAM: On-Demand Temporary Access for Humans and AI Agents

    AI agents now hand work off to other agents, risking stacked privileges and overpermissioning. Because agents plan their actions on the fly, permanent admin access means one hallucination can cascade into production. Join us on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, at 8:30 AM PST to see how Google CloudPrivileged Access Manager (PAM) brings Zero Standing Privileges to AI delegation, putting humans in command with cloud-native control that doesn't slow developers down.

    Register for the November 18 webinar
  • Streaming comes to API Gateway: real-time and AI-ready APIs

    Native streaming support is now in Public Preview for API Gateway, enabling you to run real-time and AI workloads behind your existing gateway. You can now route Server-Sent Events (SSE), WebSockets, gRPC, and chunked transfer encoding without modifying your API spec or managing a split estate. This update also strengthens integration with the Gemini platform, allowing you to stream responses from Gemini, Claude, and OpenAI gpt-oss models seamlessly while maintaining consistent authentication, rate limiting, and observability.

    Read the blog to get started

Oct 12 - Oct 16

  • AI tokenomics in action: Enforcing tiered token budgets with Apigee

    Scaling artificial intelligence across an enterprise requires clear token governance to keep LLM spend predictable across departments. Join Tarun Abraham on Thursday, November 5, 2026 for a Community TechTalk on AI tokenomics. Discover how to use Apigee to enforce isolated, tiered token budgets and model access for each team—such as assigning Engineering a dedicated budget for Gemini Pro while covering mixed usage for Marketing—without changing application code. Attendees will also gain access to a sample codebase featuring a reusable Shared Flow.

    Register for the November 5 Community TechTalk

Sept 28 - Oct 2

  • Claude Sonnet 5.5 is now available on Google Cloud. Built for focused coding and knowledge work, it delivers stronger performance for feature development, and creating presentation-ready documents, while offering more intelligence with a lower cost per task for most work at faster speed.

    Deploy Sonnet 5.5 directly from Model Garden with Google Cloud’s enterprise security, scale, and governance built in. Try it now.

  • Mastering Storage Management with Storage Intelligence

    In our new blog, explore practical strategies to modernize storage operations using Storage Intelligence Advisor and enhanced Batch Operations. See how customers like Shipt and Palo Alto Networks are using these features to manage their estates at scale. Today, Storage Intelligence is used by 25 of the top 50 GCS customers. 2 in 3 customers have Storage Intelligence enabled for over 90% of their storage footprint.

    Explore best practices on our blog
  • Cut Gen AI costs by 70% with Apigee X dynamic routing

    Generative AI deployments face a harsh cost-performance trade-off: static model selection either wastes budget or compromises quality. Discover how to build an Intelligent AI Gateway using Apigee X to dynamically evaluate prompt complexity in real-time. This new blueprint automatically routes simple queries to lightweight models (like Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite) and complex reasoning tasks to advanced models (like Gemini 3.7 Flash), achieving over 70% cost savings without sacrificing output quality.

    Read the guide to optimize your Gen AI architecture
  • AI Agent Clinic launches new hands-on session on production agent evaluations

    A new episode of the AI Agent Clinic is now available showing organizations how to move past manual "vibe checks" to build robust, production-grade agent evaluations. In this hands-on session, Google Cloud engineer Dani Zamora and Matthew Feroz (Merge) take DocsHound, an open-source LangGraph agent, and build an end-to-end eval pipeline in under an hour. Learn how to standardize multi-turn traces across any framework using OpenTelemetry and OpenInference, pair LLM judges with deterministic checkers, and catch silent quality regressions before shipping.

    Watch here
  • Drive AI impact: Join Google's Agentic Data Cloud event on Nov 4

    Every enterprise plans to adopt agentic AI within two years, but data bottlenecks hold them back—AI accesses just 45% of enterprise data today (MIT, 2026). Google's Agentic Data Cloud provides the trustworthy foundation and real-time context AI needs.Join our product leaders November 4th to explore the latest innovations across databases, analytics, business intelligence, and storage, and get direct answers in our executive Q&A with Google Data Cloud VP & GM Andi Gutmans.

    Register today!

Sept 21 - Sept 25

  • Master MCP tool authorization and agent governance with Apigee

    While the Model Context Protocol (MCP) solves interoperability for autonomous AI agents, chained actions like CRM edits or database queries quickly expose systems to unauthorized execution. Join our technical deep dive on Thursday, October 1, 2026, at 5:00 PM CEST featuring Christophe from Google Cloud. Learn how positioning Apigee between MCP clients and enterprise backends enables fine-grained authorization (FGA), complete audit trails, and policy evaluation via emerging standards like OpenID AuthZEN.

    Language and accessibility note: This session will be hosted in French, but non-French speakers can follow along seamlessly by turning on Google Meet live translated captions to read in English, Spanish, German, Portuguese, or Italian.

    Register for the October 1 Community TechTalk
  • Apigee Trace Viewer Tutorial: Capturing & Analyzing Proxy Traces

    Streamlining API proxy debugging just got easier with a new tutorial by Apigee Customer Engineer Tyler Ayers. The guide covers end-to-end instructions for capturing debug traces in both Google Cloud Apigee X (or Hybrid) and the local Apigee Emulator, extracting trace JSON data via the web UI or automated REST APIs, and analyzing execution flows, variable mutations, and latency bottlenecks using the open source Apigee Trace Viewer.

    Read the Apigee Trace Viewer guide today.
  • Automate Apigee proxy testing locally

    Catching errors early saves time and money. A new tutorial by Apigee customer engineer Tyler Ayers shows how to use the Apigee Local Emulator for automated testing. Learn to run tests locally, integrate them into CI/CD pipelines, and deploy on Google Cloud Run for shared sandboxes. This approach provides instant feedback and zero cloud costs, helping teams speed up deployment cycles.

    Read the tutorial
  • Scale your enterprise multi-agent systems with Apigee

    Deploying multi-agent architectures in production introduces critical hurdles around security, operational control, and runtime expenses. Discover how Apigee API Hub provides a central discovery surface to eliminate agent sprawl across tools, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and enterprise APIs. Learn how to turn existing backend services into secure MCP tools using Agent Gateway guardrails, while applying semantic caching and intelligent model routing to keep compounding token costs predictable.

    Join Google Cloud in Chicago in Oct.15 for The AI Evolution.Reserve your seat for Chicago
  • Automate Apigee proxy testing with the Apigee Local Emulator

    Waiting on remote deployments to validate API proxy logic slows down release cycles and increases infrastructure overhead. Join Nigel Walters on Thursday, October 8, 2026, at 5:00 PM CEST for a Community TechTalk on shift-left testing for Apigee. Discover how to use the Apigee Local Emulator and apigee-emulator-service to run sub-second assertion suites on local machines, automate CI/CD checks in GitHub Actions, and deploy ephemeral preview sandboxes on Google Cloud Run.

    Register for the October 8 Community TechTalk
  • Now in Public Preview: AI-assisted EKS-to-GKE migrations with deterministic guardrails

    Migrating complex Kubernetes estates from AWS EKS to GKE is traditionally high-friction and error-prone. Now in Public Preview, GKE Agentic Migration is an open-source agent plugin that replaces ad-hoc LLM prompting with an AI-assisted migration workflow protected by deterministic guardrails.

    Running locally in your development harness, it indexes source IaC, maps cloud-specific primitives (such as Karpenter to Custom Compute Classes), and validates configurations offline—delivering reviewable pull requests and data-migration runbooks with zero live cluster mutations.

    Learn more in theannouncement blog and try the plugin on GitHub.
  • Claude Opus 5.5 is now available on Google Cloud. Built for everyday complex tasks, it delivers stronger agentic coding, research, and analysis while handling long-running work at a lower cost per token. Google Cloud continues to provide enterprise customers with broad model choice to build, deploy, and scale their AI agents securely.

    Try ithere.
  • Import Delta Lake tables with Dataflow Job Builder!

    Migrating to borderless Lakehouse just got a lot easier. You can now import Delta Lake tables stored in Cloud Storage usingDataflow Job Builder, a no-code/low-code interface for authoring Dataflow pipelines. Because Dataflow is a fully managed service, you are spared the overhead of provisioning and managing virtual machines. For step-by-step guidance, check out the documentation here.

Sept 14 - Sept 18

  • Storage Intelligence Advisor for Google Cloud Storage is now GA

    Google Cloud Storage customers can now manage cloud storage more effectively with Storage Intelligence Advisor, delivering curated metrics, automated anomaly detection, and actionable recommendations right out of the box, with zero setup required.

    Advisor baselines activity across your projects and automatically detects four key anomalies: surges in operations, unexpected rises in cross-region egress, and spikes in errors. Each finding includes deep drill-down visibility into the resources driving the change, alongside prescriptive steps to remediate issues before they impact performance or cost.

    Learn more to get started with Storage Intelligence Advisor.
  • Build private WebSockets from Apigee X to Cloud Run

    Real-time AI agents and streaming architectures often require persistent, bidirectional connections. A new implementation guide by Apigee Customer Engineer Joel Gauci demonstrates how to establish private southbound connectivity between Apigee X and Cloud Run. Using Private Service Connect (PSC) and a Regional Internal Application Load Balancer, teams can enforce API governance and security policies at the edge while keeping backend services completely isolated from the public internet.

    Explore the step-by-step guide and open-source code
  • Connecting Gemini Enterprise Agent Runtime to Apigee with Private Service Connect 

    Deploying autonomous AI agents often presents security, compliance, and cost challenges. A new reference guide details how to build an end-to-end, private architecture between Gemini Enterprise Agent Runtime and Apigee. This design helps protect internal backends and manage token quotas.

    Read the full community guide and deploy the code
  • Discover what’s new and next in Apigee

    As enterprise architectures adapt to generative AI and autonomous workflows, Apigee is expanding its proven platform capabilities to support modern AI gateway use cases alongside traditional API management. Join our session on Thursday, September 24, featuring Apigee Product Manager Geir Sjurseth. Get an inside look at recent product releases, explore architectural patterns for securing models and agents, and bring your questions for the live Q&A.

    Register for the September 24 Apigee product update
  • Managed Service for Apache Kafka supports clusters with public Internet access!

    WithManaged Kafka public clusters, you can now produce and consume messages from clients outside your VPC—including your local machine, for faster, frictionless testing. Public clusters unlock use cases like IoT devices, retail storefronts, and telco network towers. Enable public access on new or existing clusters via the Google Cloud console, gcloud CLI, or REST API. Spin up your first public cluster, or reach out to kafka-hotline@google.com with questions.
  • Stream data directly into Bigtable using Bigtable subscriptions, now in Preview!

    You can write Pub/Sub messages to a Bigtable table with zero ETL withBigtable subscriptions. No pipelines, no code, delivered by the serverless, zero-ops experience you already know with Pub/Sub. Power your AI workloads, from model telemetry to real-time context engineering, without the overhead of managing complicated ETL pipelines. Built to be dependable, with native support for dead-letter topics. Try the feature today!

Sept 7 - Sept 10

  • Why Your Voice Agent Needs Session Auditing

    Moving voice agents to production demands robust quality monitoring. This guide dives deep into the inner workings of the Agent Development Kit (ADK) responsible for audio session auditing. Learn how the ADK's
    save_live_blob
    feature intercepts, buffers, and stores raw audio chunks during active Gemini Live sessions. We explore building an automated post-processing pipeline to seamlessly stitch these fragments into cohesive, playable audio files. Discover how to leverage these vital audio audit trails to monitor real-world interactions, diagnose failures, and ensure enterprise-grade reliability. Read the full guide here.
  • AlloyDB Omni Red Hat RPM Orchestrator now Generally Available

    AlloyDB Omni Red Hat RPM orchestrator is now Generally Available. The AlloyDB Omni Red Hat RPM orchestrator offers a new way to manage PostgreSQL-compatible workloads on bare metal or VM platforms, combining the high performance of AlloyDB, access to generative AI features and Gemini models to build AI agents and applications, and full automation. The orchestrator simplifies cluster provisioning and lifecycle management by allowing you to define reference architecture specifications, customizable by adjusting instance parameters, node configurations, and networking options — discover all details in full blog post.

Aug 31 - Sept 4

  • Automate VM guest software lifecycle with VM Extension Manager, now GA

    Google Cloud VM Extension Manager is now generally available, eliminating the need for custom startup scripts to manage guest OS extensions across Compute Engine fleets. Define declarative, project-wide policies that enforce desired software states across all regions and zones. Benefit from continuous drift detection with automatic self-healing, multi-zone phased rollouts with automated rollbacks on failure, and centralized fleet health visibility integrated with Cloud Monitoring.

    ExploreVM Extension Manager documentation
  • Assess Apigee migrations without a target environment

    Planning a migration to Apigee X or Hybrid? You can now assess your legacy Apigee Edge SaaS or OPDK environment earlier in your planning cycle. Using the updated --skip-target-validation flag in the Apigee Migration Assessment Tool, teams can generate a full inventory and establish scope baselines before target infrastructure or IAM credentials are provisioned.

    Read the guide to learn more.

  • Claude Fable 5.1 is now available on Agent Platform. It brings performance improvements over Fable 5 across reasoning, full-lifecycle coding, multi-tool workflows, and knowledge work.

    Anthropic also announced Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, a solution that gives customers the option to safely deploy Anthropic’s most capable models while storing their data in cloud infrastructure they control.

    We continue to offer enterprise customers options across frontier models to build, deploy, and scale securely on Google Cloud.

Aug 24 - Aug 28

  • Grok 4.6 is now available in Preview on Gemini Enterprise. xAI's most capable model, built for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, Grok 4.6 joins Grok 4.3 and Grok 4.20 in Model Garden and becomes the flagship of the Grok family. It supports reasoning, function calling, and structured output for multi-step agentic workflows, and accepts text and image input.

    Get started today
  • Empowering autonomous agents with advanced security governance

    AI agents offer incredible productivity gains, but granting them access to read emails, query databases, and trigger APIs introduces critical new security risks. In fact, 79% of tech leaders cite security and governance as their biggest challenge to scaling AI. Traditional tools are no longer enough to handle automated threats like prompt injection and dynamic permissions. Discover how forward-thinking enterprises are using secure-by-default design, agent identity governance, and human-in-the-loop controls to deploy agents with confidence.

    Read more
  • Stateful processing is available in BigQuery continuous queries in Preview

    Stateful operations significantly expand what’s possible with BigQuery continuous queries. This feature allows users to leverage functions like JOINs, aggregations, and windowing functions directly in their streaming queries. Now you can calculate metrics over time (for example, a 30-minute average) to power your downstream applications and AI agents with much richer, real-time signals.
  • Try out our feature here and share your feedback with bq-continuous-queries-feedback@google.com!
  • Synthetic data generator tool is available for Managed Service for Kafka

    You’ve launched your first Kafka cluster. Now what? The next thing to do is to produce some data to the cluster, but that involves modifying a client application somewhere or spinning up a virtual machine. The synthetic data generator tool, now generally available, can start sending mock data to your cluster in 3 clicks, and will get data streaming into your cluster in less than two minutes. The perfect utility for those moments you just want to test your cluster and new features. Tryour quickstart today!
  • Dataflow pipeline updates are faster & more flexible

    Dataflow pipeline updates can now stop-and-replace pipelines, a major addition to the existing in-place-update feature. The new parallel pipeline option accelerates the migration between the old & new pipeline, resulting in reduced disruption to your business. You can also set a timeout on drains that prevents runaway costs for your pipeliness in the event of stuck processing. This feature is generally available. Try it here!

Aug 17 - Aug 21

  • Webinar: Agent Identity as the backbone for secure AI innovation

    An AI agent with a stolen API key looks identical to a legitimate one. As autonomous agents scale across enterprise systems, static credentials and legacy IAM policies can no longer keep up with machine-speed execution. Join Shaun Liu, Product Manager at Google Cloud, on August 27 at 1 PM ET to explore Google Cloud’s vision for unifying agent, human, and nonhuman identity into a workload-centric platform using verifiable cryptographic identities (SPIFFE, ID-JAG, OAuth).

    Register for the webinar now

Aug 10 - Aug 14

  • Diagnosing Apigee Hybrid Cassandra Read Latency for Peak Performance

    Diagnose real-time Cassandra read latency and resolve API key verification bottlenecks in Apigee Hybrid with this step-by-step troubleshooting guide. Learn how to deploy a debugging client and query performance tables to maintain sub-millisecond response times.

    Read the Apigee Hybrid Cassandra Troubleshooting Guide
  • Keep moving with agents! The All Things Agentic Hackathon is officially live.

    We're challenging builders to build next-generation agents that take on the busy work and handle the heavy lifting in the background using Gemini 3.5 and Google Cloud. Compete for your share of $190,000 in prizes, cash, and Google Cloud credits! Submissions are open from August 3, 2026, to August 31, 2026.

    Learn more and register. Sign up for GEAR to get exclusive updates and your badge. #AllThingsAgenticHackathon
  • Accelerate PostgreSQL migrations using Gemini in Database Migration Service

    Enterprise database migrations often stall during the "last mile" of translating legacy stored procedures, triggers, and custom functions from Oracle or SQL Server. Database Migration Service (DMS) now provides AI-assisted code conversion powered by Gemini in Databases. By combining deterministic compiler rules for 1:1 syntax with Gemini contextual synthesis for complex procedural blocks, DMS converts legacy code into native PostgreSQL and AlloyDB with full schema awareness and side-by-side validation.

    Read the full blog post to learn how to streamline your database code conversion.
  • Compute Flex CUDs now available for G2 and G4 GPU VMs

    Compute Flexible Committed Use Discounts (Flex CUDs) are now available for G2 (NVIDIA L4) and G4 (NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000) VMs. You can now lock in predictable savings while retaining the flexibility to adapt across VM families, migrate between regions, and combine general-purpose compute, GKE, Cloud Run, and G2 & G4 GPU VMs under a single spend commitment. Flex CUDs for G-series VMs let you lock in savings today while preserving the agility to upgrade to latest hardware without disruption!

    Explore VM instance pricing or learn more about Flex CUDs.
  • Rapid Bucket accelerates the training and checkpoint performance in PyTorch Ecosystem via GCSFS

    With the release of GCSFS2026.8.0, organisations can now unlock maximum ROI from their AI/ML infrastructure by eliminating data starvation on GPUs in PyTorch ecosystem when they are using Frameworks like Dask, Pandas, PyTorch , PyTorch Lightning, Hugging Face Datasets, Ray dataetc. By making adaptive concurrent prefetching the default, GCSFS dynamically predicts and background-fetches sequential read patterns—boosting single-file throughput by 5x, and scaling up to 21 GiB/s , saturating the NIC when paired with Rapid Bucket. Saturating the NIC translates to significantly improved accelerator goodput and reduced training wait times with zero integration friction. Training and checkpoint restore workflows benefit from intelligent memory management that automatically drains the buffer during random reads to completely avoid bandwidth or memory penalties.

Aug 3 - Aug 7

  • Navigate data sovereignty and AI innovation with hybrid cloud

    For enterprises facing strict compliance rules, keeping sensitive data on-premises often means missing out on cutting-edge AI. Data from the 2026 State of AI Infrastructure report reveals that 52% of IT leaders are adopting hybrid cloud strategies to bridge this gap. Our latest blog post explores how Google Distributed Cloud (GDC) helps organizations deploy connected or air-gapped models to run advanced AI entirely within secure environments—mitigating geopolitical risks without sacrificing innovation.Read more.
  • SAP and Google Cloud Launch BDC Connect for BigQuery

    For years, enterprises have struggled with the cost, risk, and complexity of moving mission-critical SAP data into advanced analytics platforms. The general availability of SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC) Connect for BigQuery marks a turning point. By introducing revolutionary zero-copy, bi-directional data sharing, this new capability seamlessly bridges SAP systems with Google Cloud's powerful data and AI ecosystem. Instead of wrestling with manual data duplication and lost business context, organizations can now eliminate silos, dramatically lower their analytics costs, and rapidly deploy trustworthy, agentic AI solutions grounded in real-time operational reality.Read the full announcement to learn how to transform your data strategy.
  • Google Cloud Cortex Framework version 7 is now generally available!

    This release helps you modernize your data architecture for AI agent readiness, enabling you to quickly deploy, customize, and extend robust data products while simplifying orchestration and reducing infrastructure overhead. It providesdata product accelerators for SAP-sourced data to build trusted, high-quality data products ready for advanced analytics and agentic use cases. The Framework integrates with Google Cloud products including BigQuery, Dataform, Knowledge Catalog, and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. Learn more in our announcement blog, technical documentation, or try a demo deployment today. 
  • From API Management to AI Gateway with Apigee

    Massive LLM adoption unlocked automation but exposed critical vulnerabilities, from unpredictable token costs to security risks like prompt injection. Without central management, organizations face accelerated technical debt. Learn how to transform Apigee into an enterprise AI Gateway to centralize governance. This architectural roadmap details how to utilize semantic cache to optimize token costs, implement prompt protection policies for security, and productize tools using the emerging MCP standard.

    Read the full architectural roadmap on the Apigee Community Hub
  • Centrally govern enterprise AI traffic with Apigee AI Gateway

    Manage, track, and secure model communication across your entire infrastructure from a single pane of glass. In a new video walkthrough, Principal Architect Tyler Ayers demonstrates how Apigee AI Gateway simplifies agentic governance. Learn how to transparently proxy model traffic, log real-time token counts, and apply runtime security quotas without impacting your developer workflow.

    Watch the Apigee AI Gateway demo
  • Maximize Provisioned Throughput Utilization

    Sudden traffic micro-spikes can exceed per-second quotas, triggering 429 errors or forcing overflow into shared resource pools. A new architectural guide demonstrates how to build a serverless "shock absorber" using Cloud Run and Google Cloud Tasks. By decoupling request ingestion from execution, this queue-based pattern flattens volatile traffic bursts and smoothly drips requests to Gemini at your exact quota rate, maximizing Provisioned Throughput utilization while eliminating job failures during peak usage.Read the step-by-step setup guide.
  • Eliminate security blindspots in agentic tool interactions

    Unmonitored agentic tool calls via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) can introduce critical security risks to your enterprise architecture. Join our technical deep dive on Thursday, August 13, to discover how to position Apigee as a centralized security gateway. Featuring the new ParsePayload policy and payload operations groups in API Products, this session demonstrates how to enforce granular tool filtering, manage execution quotas, and scale secure agent ecosystems without impeding developer velocity.

    Register for the August 13 Community TechTalk

Jul 27 - Jul 31

  • Data Cloud and Apigee CDMX: The AI Agent Evolution | August 12, 2026

    Enterprise AI demands evolution beyond basic conversational assistants. To generate real value, AI models must connect with the organization's core systems and live data sources. Join us this August 12 at Google CDMX for the exclusive event AI Evolution: Powering Tomorrow's Enterprise. Learn how to design an agile and secure ecosystem by unifying the power of Gemini, Apigee, and data agent technologies through practical demonstrations led by Google Cloud engineers.

    Secure your spot for the in-person session in Mexico CityRegister now!
  • Vast Edge, built on GCP, launches the first live recovery interface for cloud backups, enabling IT teams to inspect backup contents in real time. This transforms backups from a blind, log-based process into an interactive platform where teams can instantly search, preview, and validate the exact data available for restore.

    This platform protects Google Workspace, NetSuite, Salesforce, Workday and many SaaS environments, providing complete visibility and enterprise-grade oversight.

    VisitVast Edge Backup & Disaster Recovery and get a free trial of their backup solutions on the GCP Marketplace for Google Workspace Backup, NetSuite Backup, Salesforce Backup, and Workday Backup.

Jul 20 - Jul 24

  • Claude Opus 5, Anthropic’s latest model, is now available on Agent Platform. It brings performance improvements over Opus 4.8 across coding, long-running agents, and knowledge work.The model is Zero Data Retention (ZDR) compatible. For safety, high-risk workflows — such as penetration testing or exploit generation — it will notify you and fall back to Opus 4.8.We’re excited to continue to offer enterprise customers options across frontier models to build, deploy, and scale AI securely. Try it here. 
  • Apigee Northam Roadshow 2026 | The AI Agent Evolution: Powering Tomorrow's Enterprise

    AI is evolving. As your organization deploys autonomous agents, the integration between APIs and models becomes critical. Join Google Cloud specialists for an exclusive day of deep-dive sessions and live demos. Discover how the unified power of Apigee and the Google Cloud Agent Platform allows you to build, govern, and scale high-performance AI agents with complete control. Call to Action:Register for Sunnyvale | Register for NYC | Register for Chicago
  • Deploy an Apigee Proxy for MCP Registry Discovery  

    Learn how to deploy an Apigee X proxy to format Apigee API Hub data into the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Registry format. This tutorial by Tyler Ayers guides developers through cloning the sample repository, deploying using the Apigee Feature Templater (aft), and testing the endpoint to make API data easily discoverable by coding agents.

    Read the full community tutorial to get started.
  • Simplify AI Infrastructure: Getting Started with Apigee AI Gateway

    Managing a complex AI landscape with multiple backend environments can present significant operational and governance challenges. A new tutorial walks you through how to build a unified API proxy using Apigee AI Gateway. By establishing a single, secure entry point for all model traffic, teams gain access to real-time analytics, comprehensive tracing, and financial operations auditing—completely seamlessly, and with absolutely no modifications required to client environments or user configurations.

    Read the step-by-step setup guide
  • Your AI agents are ready. Is your data?

    The biggest bottleneck to scaling AI isn't the models—it's giving them access to business context. As enterprises move to proactive systems of action, legacy infrastructure often buckles under the nonlinear speed of AI agents. Google Cloud’s new Agentic Data Cloud, built on AI-native infrastructure, solves this by unifying data, AI models, and operational databases. Discover how a borderless Lakehouse and active Knowledge Catalog can empower your AI agents with trusted, real-time context without unnecessary engineering overhead.Read more.
  • Secure and govern your AI at Apigee AI Horizon in London

    Moving AI from basic prompts to complex agentic workflows requires trust and control. Join us on Tuesday, 1st September 2026 at Google London for our 5th edition of Apigee AI Horizon. Discover how Google Cloud product leaders and architects are using Apigee and Model Armor to secure LLM APIs, implement policy controls, and manage token consumption. Do not miss this one—register soon!

    Secure your spot for AI Horizon London

Jul 13 - Jul 17

  • Resource-Based CUD Sharing is Now Enabled by Default

    Starting June 16, 2026, the default setting for Google Cloud Resource-based Committed Use Discount (CUD) sharing will change from disabled to enabled for new billing accounts and eligible existing accounts without active CUDs. This update automatically maximizes your savings by pooling underutilized discounts across your resources.

    You retain full control and can adjust your CUD sharing preferences at any time by changing your CUD scope configuration. For instructions, seeEnable CUD sharing or Disable CUD sharing.
  • Webinar for India: Google Cloud for EdTech: Optimizing Traffic and Token Governance at Scale

    API traffic surges and AI model integration are reshaping the EdTech landscape. Join Satyam Maloo for the webinar Google Cloud for EdTech: Optimizing Traffic and Token Governance at Scale on July 23, 2026. Learn to implement advanced rate limiting, gain granular token visibility, and leverage real-time analytics to govern your platform effectively. Whether you’re scaling for peak academic seasons or integrating complex AI workflows, this session provides the infrastructure blueprint you need.

    Register Now
  • Scaling AI Agents: Treat prompts like software artifacts

    As AI agents move into production, monolithic system prompts often result in configuration drift, merge conflicts, and silent runtime failures. The solution is adopting a Prompts-as-Code architecture. By breaking prompts into modular skill files and using a build-time transpiler, engineering teams can introduce dependency resolution, static validation, and CI/CD rigor to their agent's control plane. Stop manually editing massive text files and start building deterministic, reliable agent infrastructure.

    Read morehere.

entries.content:

Product Management

Today, we’re excited to announce the general availability of our next-generation Storage-optimized Z4M machine series in Google Compute Engine, available as both Virtual Machine (VM) and bare-metal instances. 

We built Z4M to provide storage for AI/ML training and inference workloads such as checkpointing, distributed key-value (KV) cache and parallel file systems — workloads that handle huge data volumes and require massive parallel data processing, as well as high storage and networking throughput. Low latency access to data is equally critical to keep GPUs and TPUs fully utilized. Powered by the fifth-generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors and paired with the latest enhancements in Titanium, Z4M provides up to 168,000 GiB of Local SSD (LSSD) storage coupled with up to 400 Gbps of Cloud Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) networking. RDMA improves the performance of these demanding workloads by reducing data-access latency by up to 60% compared to TCP networking, so you can increase your applications’ throughput while right-sizing your cloud investment. 

Z4M VMs and bare-metal instances

The Z4M VM portfolio lets you scale your infrastructure and clusters to meet workload requirements by providing a large total LSSD capacity as well as 875 GiB of LSSD capacity per vCPU. Further, Z4M bare-metal instances give you direct access to the physical hardware without a virtualization layer, reducing latency for workloads such as custom hypervisors and workloads with specific licensing needs. Z4M bare-metal instances are also ideal for agentic AI workloads, enabling developers to run isolated sandboxes at scale, including with Agent Substrate.

In addition to 168,000 GiB of LSSD storage, Z4M VMs and bare metal instances offer up to 192 vCPUs and up to 1,536 GiB of memory for at-scale data processing. Z4M instances are based on Titanium SSDs, which offload local storage processing from CPU resources to deliver real-time data processing, low-latency, high-throughput storage performance and enhanced storage security. Z4M delivers up to 15.6M random-read IOPS and up to 75,600 MiB/s sequential-read throughput, improving the LSSD storage performance and throughput compared to Z3 by up to 70% and 110% respectively. 

Cloud RDMA and direct storage access

Z4M provides low-latency access to the storage layer using 400 Gbps of RDMA-enabled standard networking.This helps keep GPUs and TPUs fully utilized even when processing large multimodal datasets, by transferring massive amounts of data at line rate using NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage and TPUDirect Storage. At the same time, Z4M transfers data at full line rate while processing data locally, with a balanced-LSSD-to-networking-throughput ratio of 1.4:1. 

Built for demanding workloads

What customers and partners are saying

"Nutanix is committed to helping organizations run their applications and data anywhere. Bringing Nutanix Cloud Clusters (NC2) to Google Cloud's new Z4M metal instances reflects that mission and our continued partnership with Google Cloud. By combining Z4M’s exceptional I/O performance and high storage density along with Intel’s advanced compute and AMX-driven efficiency, NC2 on Z4M provides the scale, density, and performance required to power everything from dense VDI clusters to demanding, data-intensive AI workloads." - Saveen Pakala, Vice President of Product Management, Nutanix

"Google's Z4M VMs bring Cloud RDMA to a storage-optimized VM with much higher local SSD density than previous generations. In our testing, Cloud RDMA on Z4M demonstrated outstanding performance with up to 3.7x lower latency and up to 6x lower CPU usage than TCP. For our customers, that means faster, more predictable performance across a wide variety of use cases, from I/O-intensive databases to analytics and AI workloads, with the storage density to scale capacity efficiently." - Adik Sokolovski, Chief R&D Officer, Silk

“We're excited to support Google Cloud's new Z4M platform as part of the Sycomp Intelligent Data Storage Platform. With greater capacity per node and the continued evolution of the Z-series architecture, Z4M helps customers achieve new levels of performance and efficiency. Supporting innovations like Z4M reinforces Sycomp's commitment to delivering high-performance storage solutions across the Google Cloud ecosystem.” - Scott Fadden, Senior HPC Solutions Architect, Sycomp

"We've worked alongside Google Cloud for years on the most demanding AI and machine learning workloads. In our testing, we found the new Z4M machines deliver roughly twice the read throughput and up to 79% more IOPS, generation over generation (Z3 family). This means more data, more tokens, and more finished work. We’re excited to see what our joint customers build with these powerful machines." - Ajay Singh, Chief Product Officer, WEKA

Orchestration with Cluster Director

You can easily configure, deploy and manage large Z4M clusters using Google Cloud’s Cluster Director, which offers advanced placement and maintenance capabilities alongside the Cluster Toolkit for rapid cluster deployment. You can view and deploy your workloads in a compact topology to maximize performance, or spread topology for high availability by targeting availability domains. You can combine or stagger the maintenance across these availability domains. Additionally, you can co-locate Z4M instances with your GPU and TPU clusters to process very large datasets in real time and at scale. 

Enhanced maintenance experience

Both Z4M VMs and bare-metal instances make it easier for you to plan ahead and schedule maintenance operations by providing notice from the system several days in advance of required maintenance. For Z4M VMs with 42,000 GiB or less of LSSD storage, you can live-migrate an instance during maintenance events. Z4M VMs with 84,000 GiB or more of LSSD and Z4M bare metal instances must be terminated and restarted while preserving your data through planned maintenance events.

Support for Hyperdisk

Z4M VMs and bare-metal instances support Hyperdisk, Google Cloud’s workload-optimized block storage, which lets you optimize the performance for each workload by independently tuning the storage performance and capacity for each instance.

Specifically, they are compatible with Hyperdisk Balanced, Hyperdisk Throughput, and Extreme Hyperdisk storage for scalable, high-performance network-attached storage, supporting up to 512 TiB of capacity per instance. For general-purpose workloads, Hyperdisk Balanced, with up to 320K IOPS per instance, offers a mix of performance and cost-efficiency. Hyperdisk Extreme delivers ultra-low latency and supports up to 500K IOPS and 12,500 MiB/s throughput per Z4M VM and bare-metal instance, making it well-suited for demanding database workloads. 

Get started with Z4M today

Z4M VMs and bare metal instances are available today in select regions worldwide. To start using Z4M instances, choose Z4M under the Storage-Optimized machine family when creating a new VM or GKE node pool in the Google Cloud console. Learn more at the Z4M machine series page. Contact your Google Cloud sales representative for more information on regional availability.

AI is rapidly transforming video production at virtually every step of the process, from ideation and storyboarding to filming, editing, and
entries.content:
Iñaki Berenguer

CEO, Mito

Keyvan Akbary

Head of Engineering, Mito

Welcome back to The Blueprint, a regular feature where we highlight how Google Cloud customers are tackling unique and common challenges across industries using the latest AI and cloud technologies. We hope to inspire others looking to innovate in their work.

AI is rapidly transforming video production at virtually every step of the process, from ideation and storyboarding to filming, editing, and release. At Mito, we’re striving to democratize AI-powered video creation, enabling everyone from solo artists to large enterprises to get the most out of the best creative technologies available.

The Challenge

When we founded Mito, our goal was to eliminate the complex technical friction that stops creators from telling long-form, narrative stories with generative AI.

However, transitioning from a single five-second clip to a cohesive campaign — such as a 120-second national TV spot for Movistar Plus+, a part of Telefónica, to broadcast across Spain during the World Cup this summer. This effort revealed massive infrastructure and workflow bottlenecks:

  • Asset & workflow overhead: Managing local media libraries across individual workstations was unscalable. For Movistar alone, our production required generating a massive "iceberg" of over 5000 assets (1000 of those videos) generated in around 65 iteration rounds.

  • Zero real-time collaboration: Traditional feedback loops required manual downloads, Google Drive uploads, and fragmented communication across chat apps and email.

  • Rendering latency: Standard AI video rendering takes four to five minutes per short clip. Running these processes synchronously froze our user interface and stalled creative velocity.

  • Model disparity & consistency: Every generative model requires distinct prompting logic. Maintaining character persistence, specific lighting, and camera angles across dozens of shots — while preserving the likeness of real public figures like chef Ferran Adrià or journalist Juanma Castaño — was nearly impossible without central orchestration.

  • Capacity constraints: Operating on public pay-as-you-go model APIs left us vulnerable to rate limits and regional throughput throttling during peak traffic.

The Solution

To deliver an infinite, real-time creative canvas for filmmakers, we designed a serverless, asynchronous architecture built on Google Cloud.

We run our API, AI Director, and background workers as Java services on Cloud Run, which scales with request volume.

In order to address message routing challenges, we decoupled job execution using Google Cloud Pub/Sub as our central event bus. Long-running video generations are offloaded to background Cloud Run workers, allowing creators to keep working uninterrupted on the UI canvas.

To minimize latency, media assets are stored in Google Cloud Storage and delivered via Cloud CDN. Expiring key signatures keep pre-release client assets strictly private. Keeping our storage alongside the models we call through Vertex AI reduces network transfer delays.

An isolated database architecture helps with the heavy business intelligence and analytics workloads while mitigating potential negative impacts on production performance through Cloud SQL and PostgreSQL. We rely heavily on foundational models like Omni, Veo and Nano Banana, which we access through Vertex AI alongside our custom system prompts.

Finally, our structured canvas frontend enforces a "Rule of 6" (limiting prompt variables across World, Camera, Light, Texture, Actions, and Character) and prioritizes still-frame generation before video rendering to maximize cost efficiency.

The Architecture

The Outcome

By pairing our creative orchestration platform with Google Cloud’s infrastructure, we successfully delivered a landmark national broadcast campaign that the production team describes as 95% AI-generated:

  • Prime-time scale: The 120-second Movistar campaign for the Spanish National Team aired across every major television channel in Spain, with 1,441 assets live on a single shared Canvas near launch.

  • AI Director copilot: Our conversational agent translates natural language instructions into precise model parameters while maintaining context, lighting, and visual style across every scene.

  • Seamless collaboration: Distributed teams and brand clients can work on the same canvas in real time. Because new generations are saved as separate assets instead of overwriting earlier ones, stakeholders can duplicate projects to explore parallel creative ideas.

  • Continuous dogfooding: Through our internal studio, Mito Films, we put our tools to the test on high-stakes client projects — whether that's global television spots or keynotes for top robotics startups — ensuring direct feedback flows back into engineering.

  • Future-proof foundation: Our architecture is primed for rendering times to collapse from minutes to seconds, positioning Mito to handle upcoming world models, deeper memory states, and personalized content delivery.

The Details

Building an enterprise-grade platform for AI storytelling required solving several backend and creative challenges. This includes our creation of a virtual queuing system that mitigates third-party API rate limiting during usage spikes for smooth request concurrency, with bounded retries and a clear outcome for every job.

Because creative output cannot be fully validated with standard unit tests, we built an automated evaluation harness powered by Gemini. Acting as an independent judge, it evaluates AI Director outputs against original user intents across an automated test suite, which we run alongside standard tests for high-impact Director changes.

We knew early on that we would need multi-model intelligence routing. As such, we built the AI Director to dynamically coordinate tasks across multiple specialized models — including Sonnet, Gemini, and ElevenLabs for audio — treating the spatial canvas like a live code repository to infer adjacent contextual cues.

We also needed to embrace an “imperfect aesthetic” to arrive at a more authentic outcome. In our Movistar spot, the story follows Tommy, a 17-year-old student making an AI video project. At the climax, the AI misunderstands a prompt, making coach Luis de la Fuente say "In the same milkshake" while holding a drink. Tommy edits the prompt live to "In the same heartbeat," and the video recalibrates instantly.

By incorporating surreal visual elements — like stadium stands built into Galician cliffs or a neighborhood bar covered in pitch grass — we showcased how generative AI can elevate human storytelling rather than obscure it.

entries.content:
Shenyang Cai

Senior Software Engineer

Imagine running advanced machine learning workflows—from forecasting and classification to high-dimensional embedding generation—without ever leaving your familiar pandas DataFrame. With the new 

.bigquery
accessor from BigQuery DataFrames (BigFrames), that vision is now a reality. You can seamlessly invoke BigQuery's enterprise-grade AI functions directly within pandas, scaling your data science and ML pipelines on cloud infrastructure .

Take linear regression as an example. Traditionally, a pandas user who needs to run regression would have to extract data locally, manually select features, and train a custom scikit-learn model like this:

Now, with the 

.bigquery
accessor, you can bypass the local training process entirely and leverage powerful 
ai.predict()
directly on your data in BigQuery:

As you can see, the 

ai.predict()
is able to perform regression tasks directly over two pandas dataframes with a single function call, which greatly simplifies the entire ML process.

How the BigQuery accessor works

Under the hood, the 

.bigquery
accessor uses BigQuery DataFrames library to transparently push your computations to Google Cloud. When you call an AI method like 
.ai.predict()
, it doesn't compute the regression locally. Instead, it translates the pandas operation into Google Standard SQL, executes the corresponding foundational model (like TabFM) natively on BigQuery's infrastructure, and seamlessly returns the result as a standard pandas DataFrame. This allows you to easily process local datasets with powerful offerings unique to BigQuery.

The following sections detail additional executable code examples. You can also find them all in this notebook.

Environment setup

Before executing the code samples in this post, ensure you have a Google Cloud project with the following roles granted (see more at permissions for AI functions):

  • Run query jobs: BigQuery Job User (roles/bigquery.jobUser)

  • Access a foundation model in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform: Agent Platform User (roles/aiplatform.user)

Next, install pandas and bigframes in your Jupyter environment. To enable the AI accessors, simply import the bigframes library and specify your Google Cloud project ID. This ensures all subsequent AI function calls are routed through your authorized project:

Once configured, you can call BigQuery AI functions directly on standard pandas objects.

Functions on pandas series

AI functions attached to a pandas `Series` accept single-column input sequences.

Example: AI.EMBED

Generating vector embeddings is a fundamental step in many modern NLP and semantic search pipelines. By using the `ai.embed()` function, you can compute embeddings for an entire column of text in a single, clean expression.

Behind the scenes, BigFrames converts the pandas Series for processing in BigQuery and casts the output back into a native pandas Series. From the developer’s perspective, the workflow remains entirely within pandas.

Notice that the output of this operation is a native pandas `Series` containing the resulting embedding list. BigFrames handles the temporary BigQuery conversions, model execution, and final data formatting, ensuring that you never have to leave your familiar pandas interface.

Example: AI.SIMILARITY

When you need to calculate semantic closeness, the `ai.similarity()` function computes cosine similarity scores between your series elements and a target. This target can be either a scalar literal string or another series. Here is how you can compare a pandas `Series` against a scalar string to find matching concepts:

Similarly, you can perform pairwise comparisons between two distinct pandas `Series` objects to find semantic correlations across different datasets:

In both cases, the returned object is a standard pandas `Series` with floating-point similarity scores, making it immediately compatible with downstream pandas methods like filtering or sorting.

Functions on pandas DataFrames

DataFrame AI functions operate on multi-column structured tables or handle complex prompts involving multiple data inputs.

Example: AI.FORECAST

Time-series forecasting typically requires a lot of boilerplate code to format timestamps, group entities, and train a model. The `ai.forecast()` function performs time-series forecasting across grouped structured data with simple, high-level parameters. To demonstrate this, you first prepare the input sample DataFrame representing historical sales data:

With your data prepared, you can call `ai.forecast()` directly on the DataFrame. Here, you specify the target metric, timestamp column, grouping key, and a prediction horizon of three days:

The returned DataFrame provides complete forecast values alongside statistical parameters such as confidence levels and prediction intervals. Internally, this triggers a TimesFM model that performs the trend analysis, returning neatly structured results back to your local environment as a pandas DataFrame. You can also choose the model version with the model argument. For example, pass model="TimesFM 3.0" to use the newest TimesFM model, now in Preview in BigQuery, which ranks #1 on the GIFT-Eval, FEV-Bench, and TIME forecasting benchmarks.

Example: AI.IF

Filtering rows on a natural-language condition is one of the most common generative AI tasks. The `ai.if_()` function evaluates a prompt built from literal strings and DataFrame columns, and returns True or False for each row:

Because `ai.if_()` returns a boolean Series, you can use it directly as a pandas filter mask, for example `df[df.bigquery.ai.if_(prompt)]`. `ai.if_()` runs in optimized mode by default (optimization_mode="minimize_cost"): a local, distilled model processes the majority of rows, and only the rest are sent to Gemini, which reduces cost and latency on large datasets. To send every row to the LLM instead, set `optimization_mode` to `"maximize_quality"`.

Get started

The AI functions provided by 

bigquery
accessor unlock advanced machine learning tools directly inside your native data structures, enabling you to solve complex AI challenges without leaving the Python ecosystem you already know.

Currently supported AI functions include the following (see the documentation for full details):

Pandas Series

  • embed(): Generates vector embeddings to a single column.

  • generate_embedding(): Generates vector embeddings to a table.

  • generate_table(): Performs natural language tasks and generates structured outputs.

  • generate_text(): Performs natural language tasks and generates free-form texts.

  • similarity(): Computes semantic closeness (cosine similarity) between entries.

Pandas DataFrame

  • classify(): Performs zero-shot classification.

  • forecast(): Runs time-series forecasting across grouped data using TimesFM, including the new TimesFM 3.0.

  • generate(): Evaluates dynamic prompts across multiple columns to generate text responses.

  • generate_bool(): Evaluates natural language conditions and returns booleans (True/False).

  • generate_double(): Evaluates a prompt and returns floating-point numbers.

  • generate_int(): Evaluates a prompt and returns integers.

  • if_(): Filters rows on a natural-language condition, using optimized mode by default to reduce cost and latency.

  • predict(): Runs predictive modeling, such as regression, using TabFM.

  • score(): Rates inputs based on a scoring system that you described.

Whether you want to generate embeddings or run full time-series forecasts, BigQuery AI functions inside pandas make scaling machine learning effortless. Give it a spin and let your data do the heavy lifting!

entries.title: Bringing conversational analytics to Gemini with Agentic Data Cloud connectors

Across most organizations, data questions multiply faster than analysts can answer them: Projects stall in ticket queues, leaders fall back on guesswork, and unmanaged spreadsheets spread across teams. Early generative AI tools promised conv
entries.content:
Leigha Reid

Senior Product Manager, Data Cloud

Mohsin Imam

Senior Product Manager, Data Cloud

Data Cloud connectors in Gemini for business, now in preview, give business users and analysts a direct way to query live enterprise data in natural language. Across most organizations, data questions multiply faster than analysts can answer them: Projects stall in ticket queues, leaders fall back on guesswork, and unmanaged spreadsheets spread across teams. Early generative AI tools promised conversational access to data, but they often struggled to generate accurate SQL across complex schemas or to respect governance rules. Data Cloud connectors let you query governed data directly from your workspace while enforcing row- and column-level security and respecting end-user credentials.

A new way to query enterprise data

Gemini brings conversational analytics directly into your day-to-day workflow through two paths: Conversational Analytics agents, which let you create data agents that include context and instructions to effectively answer questions for specific use cases, and Data Cloud connectors, allowing you to query live data directly with Gemini. End users can pull data directly from BigQuery (preview), operational databases like Spanner, AlloyDB, and Cloud SQL (preview), and governed data from Looker (preview). From there, you can move your findings directly into everyday tools, such as turning query results into a Google Doc, an email draft in Gmail, or a deck in Google Slides.

Ask natural-language questions across enterprise data using Data Cloud connectors.

How Data Cloud connectors work

Data Cloud connectors work with Knowledge Catalog to locate relevant data, interpret your question, and execute permission-scoped queries under your identity.

Knowledge Catalog interprets the user prompt and identifies the right data source for the query.

When you ask a question in Gemini, the system coordinates discovery, semantic interpretation, and query execution, using the following capabilities:

  • Natural-language question: You ask an exploratory question in plain language (for example, "How many sales did we have this month for all cold weather products?"). End users aren’t expected to know the table or project to use.

  • Semantic discovery: Gemini searches Knowledge Catalog to locate candidate data across your estate, considering key attributes like usage patterns.

  • Context mapping: The system uses technical metadata, business glossaries, and semantic models to map everyday terms into exact database structures, such as resolving "cold weather products" to specific categories like sweaters, coats, and jackets in an ecommerce catalog.

  • Permission-aware execution: Gemini generates a SQL query and runs it through the connector under your user credentials, respecting your existing row- and column-level database permissions.

Step-by-step flow of a user prompt from Gemini to query execution.

To accurately navigate an enterprise data estate, language models need business context alongside raw database access. Knowledge Catalog provides a curated context bundle, including technical metadata, business logic, table relationships, and verified queries, that improves query accuracy while reducing latency and token consumption.

Navigating the context graph visually in Knowledge Catalog.

Enterprise analytics has long been fragmented by physical borders: data locked in proprietary silos, open lakehouse tables in cloud object storage, and datasets distributed across multicloud environments. Beyond native BigQuery storage, the BigQuery connector brings conversational analytics to a borderless lakehouse, unifying these environments into a single conversational interface to query open table formats (including Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, and Parquet) and cross-cloud datasets in AWS or Azure using BigQuery. The connector inherits fine-grained access policies from BigQuery and Knowledge Catalog, so row- and column-level access controls apply whether you query native tables or open lakehouse files.

Gemini accesses data across BigQuery and AWS S3 (through the AWS Glue federated catalog) to answer questions in plain language.

Choosing between connectors and data agents

In addition to using direct Data Cloud connectors to query data in plain language, you can also use Conversational Analytics agents to enable these experiences. While Data Cloud connectors allow you to provide exploratory and ad hoc analysis for users, conversational analytics agents are scoped agents that are built and certified directly by data teams within your organization. These can be built across Data Cloud products such as BigQuery, Looker, and operational databases including Spanner, AlloyDB, and Cloud SQL.

These pre-configured agents allow users to run highly governed, multi-step strategic analyses that are scoped to particular subsets of data, supporting compliance requirements and predictable results for reporting. These data agents can also be published in Gemini for consumption or made available via API for building your own conversational apps in the enterprise.

These approaches are complementary. Gemini direct connectivity also surfaces relevant published agents created by central data teams, so users can decide whether to proceed with ad hoc analysis using the connectors or use the scoped agent. You can choose the right approach for each workload.

Built-in access controls and governance

Data Cloud connector queries execute under the end user’s identity. An employee without access to executive salary data or protected healthcare records cannot query that data through natural-language prompts. The agent only discovers metadata in Knowledge Catalog to which you have access, and only executes queries that your account has permission to run.

How to create Data Cloud connectors

Administrators can configure Data Cloud connectors in the Gemini admin console. From there, admins set up default read-only connections to datasets in BigQuery, operational databases, or Looker, with Knowledge Catalog enabled automatically. Once configured, end users can enable the connector in Gemini to start querying data and building reports in plain language.

Create a connected data store in Gemini and authorize it on first use.

Setup documentation is available for the BigQuery, Spanner, Cloud SQL, and AlloyDB for PostgreSQL connectors, with Looker also in preview.

Unlike data ingestion mode, which copies data into a Gemini data store, Data Cloud connectors use federated query mode to query your data in place without copying or indexing it — using Knowledge Catalog automatically to search accessible metadata and look up business context.

Why use Data Cloud connectors over custom MCP

Compared to connecting to public or self-managed Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, first-party Data Cloud connectors provide two main advantages:

  • Built-in skills for higher response quality: Data Cloud connectors include pre-configured agent skills tailored to each data engine, such as advanced SQL and AI function generation for BigQuery and operational databases, to improve query accuracy and response quality.

  • Guided setup and managed authentication: First-party connectors provide a guided setup experience with managed authentication for Google Cloud databases and BigQuery, removing the need to deploy MCP middleware or manage your own OAuth client configuration for Google Cloud services. In addition, connector-specific settings, such as specifying a default Google Cloud billing project for BigQuery query execution, help administrators enforce governance and manage query costs.

Get started today

Data Cloud connectors help teams find answers from enterprise data sources without waiting on backlog queues. To get started, review the Data Cloud connectors documentation or explore Conversational Analytics agents.

entries.title: Semantic aggregation over millions of rows in BigQuery with AI.AGG
entries.summary: For more than a decade, BigQuery has helped set standards for structured data aggregation, calculating financial sums, counting active users, and computing historical averages at a petabyte scale in seconds. But as modern enterprises become inundated with unstructured data — application logs, customer service transcripts, product imagery, and diagnostic reports — a critical gap has emerged. Histor
entries.content:
Pramod Niralakeri

Strategic Cloud Engineer

Shruti Malgatti

Cloud Migration Consultant, Data

For more than a decade, BigQuery has helped set standards for structured data aggregation, calculating financial sums, counting active users, and computing historical averages at a petabyte scale in seconds. But as modern enterprises become inundated with unstructured data — application logs, customer service transcripts, product imagery, and diagnostic reports — a critical gap has emerged.

Historically, relational SQL engines have lacked the native ability to aggregate, synthesize, and extract overarching semantic themes from millions of rows of text and multimodal data. While BigQuery recently introduced powerful row-level AI functions (like AI.GENERATE and AI.CLASSIFY), analyzing massive datasets holistically presents a unique architectural challenge: the large language model (LLM) context window.

Even with advanced foundation models like Gemini, you cannot pass millions of rows into a single prompt without triggering severe truncation or hard execution failures. Traditionally, solving this required data engineering teams to construct complex external map-reduce pipelines, manage rate-limiting backoffs, and recursively stitch chunked summaries together.

Today, we are thrilled to deep-dive into AI.AGG — currently in preview — a fully managed, multi-level semantic aggregation function natively embedded within BigQuery GoogleSQL. By conceptualizing semantic aggregation as a distributed map-reduce problem, AI.AGG enables data teams to run natural-language instructions over millions of rows of data using a single SQL query.

Here is a look under the hood at how it works, transformative enterprise use cases, and best practices for deploying it in production.

Turning petabytes of data into semantic insights natively in BigQuery.

Multi-level batching architecture

AI.AGG
abstracts the immense engineering complexity of chunking and parallel execution. When you execute an 
AI.AGG
query, the BigQuery engine automatically orchestrates a sequence natively within the database:

  • Row-level validation: The engine helps verify no single row exceeds the maximum context window (dropping or returning an error on payloads >10 MiB).

  • Context-safe batching: The engine dynamically groups input rows into smaller batches that safely fit within the token limits of your chosen Gemini endpoint.

  • Parallel inference: Your natural-language SQL prompt is applied to each batch in parallel, generating intermediate semantic summaries via Vertex AI.

  • Recursive synthesis: Finally, the system batches these intermediate outputs together and passes them back to the LLM with the exact same instruction. This reduction repeats recursively until a single, final aggregated string is produced per SQL 

    GROUP BY
    clause.

Because 

AI.AGG
requires deep reasoning to synthesize concepts across disparate batches, it relies entirely on full-weight LLMs for every stage of its pipeline — differentiating it from row-level functions like 
AI.CLASSIFY
, which can leverage distilled CPU proxy models.

Built for the multimodal enterprise

AI.AGG
natively supports both text and multimodal inputs. By leveraging BigQuery Object Tables and the 
OBJ.GET_ACCESS_URL
function, analytics teams can aggregate visual insights across thousands of images stored directly in Cloud Storage with no data movement or transcoding required.

Data engineering pro-tip: The NULL exclusivity rule

When evaluating multiple columns, users often pass a STRUCT into the function. However, if even a single field within that composite structure evaluates to NULL, the entire row is treated as NULL and silently discarded. Always explicitly wrap nullable fields with IFNULL() (e.g., IFNULL(description, 'No data provided')) to help verify your data safely enters the pipeline.

Transformative enterprise use cases

The true analytical power of 

AI.AGG
emerges when combined with standard SQL 
GROUP BY
operations.

1. Diagnostic analysis of high-volume system logs

System logs generated by globally distributed microservices often hide subtle degradations (like memory thrashing or systemic clock drift) that never throw explicit fatal errors. Using 

AI.AGG
, DevOps teams can group millions of logs by system component and generate targeted, human-readable diagnostic summaries.

  • Prompting Tip: Instruct the model to explicitly describe the "normal operation" of the component before hunting for anomalies. This helps suppress the LLM's tendency to hallucinate errors on completely healthy logs.

2. Building the "agentic data cloud"

AI.AGG
isn't just an analytical reporting tool; it’s a dynamic orchestration engine. Imagine acquiring a massive repository of legacy support tickets with no clear categorization. You can deploy 
AI.AGG
to read the raw text, synthesize a definitive list of categories, and output them as a strict JSON array.

By unpacking this array via 

JSON_VALUE_ARRAY
and feeding those dynamic labels directly into row-level classifiers like 
AI.CLASSIFY
, you can orchestrate an end-to-end, autonomous data labeling pipeline natively in SQL — reducing the need for external Python scripts.

Prompt engineering is data engineering

When integrating generative models into highly deterministic SQL pipelines, standard conversational prompts will often fail. Prompting for programmatic SQL outputs is a strict engineering discipline:

  • Explicit output contracts: Treat the prompt as an API contract. Append commands like: "Return exactly one valid JSON array of strings. Do not include markdown code blocks or conversational text."

  • Contextual delimiters: Use string concatenation with explicit labels (e.g., 

    '- Description: '
    ) to anchor the LLM and prevent it from conflating fields across dense batches.

  • Failure state design: Explicitly instruct the model to return strict null values for missing information rather than guessing, preventing schema hallucinations downstream.

  • Few-shot anchoring: Provide a literal example of your expected structure within the prompt to heavily ground the model's attention mechanism.

Governance, cost management, and guardrails

Transitioning semantic workloads to production requires operational oversight. Because of the recursive batching architecture, the total tokens sent to Gemini will be greater than the token count of your source data. To mitigate costs, mandate strict 

WHERE
and 
LIMIT
pre-filtering.

Furthermore, for workflows cross-referencing massive, static datasets, BigQuery supports Gemini Context Caching, which can reduce input token costs and execution latency. Use the 

AI.COUNT_TOKENS
utility to estimate query costs prior to execution.

Administrators can operate knowing 

AI.AGG
works strictly within BigQuery's governance framework, supporting VPC Service Controls (VPC-SC) to prevent data exfiltration. Furthermore, if a transient error occurs during a batch process, the function degrades gracefully — skipping the rejected rows rather than crashing the entire query.

Preview guardrails to keep in mind:

  • The final output string per SQL group is strictly capped at 10,000 tokens per group. Ask the model for concise output

  • Individual payload rows must not exceed 10 MiB.

  • When processing multimodal arrays, limit image assets to fewer than 10 images per row to avoid silent skipping.

For optimal stability, we recommend processing a maximum of 20 million rows and outputting a maximum of 1,000 distinct SQL groups per query.

Putting AI.AGG into practice

To help you get started, here are examples of how 

AI.AGG
is used to synthesize insights alongside traditional SQL metrics.

Macro-level topic discovery

Summarize what specific top authors talk about, turning thousands of their comments into a concise narrative

Autonomous diagnostic reporting for DevOps (log analysis)

Instead of counting standard HTTP error codes, use 

AI.AGG
to read thousands of raw stack traces and log messages, grouping them by the microservice name to find the qualitative root cause of systemic failures.

The next era of the data warehouse

With 

AI.AGG
, Google Cloud is democratizing access to semantic analysis at petabyte scale. By marrying the deterministic grouping power of BigQuery’s relational engine with the macroscopic reasoning capabilities of Vertex AI Gemini, we are transforming the enterprise data warehouse from a passive repository of historical metrics into an active, semantic runtime capable of deep, holistic intelligence.

Ready to unlock the semantic value of your enterprise data? Head over to the Google Cloud console, explore the BigQuery documentation, and run your first semantic aggregation today.

entries.content:
John Nack

Sr. Product Manager, Google Cloud

Today, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is generally available on Google Cloud. Built for the everyday videos businesses make in volume — like product videos, virtual try-ons, and ads — this model is fast, cost-effective, and follows your image, video and audio references more closely than before.

Business users can create with it in Gemini for business and Google Vids, and developers can build with it via API.

Here's what's new:

  • A lower price: $0.07 per second of 720p video, 30% less than Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, with similar savings at other resolutions.
  • Longer clips: Generate and edit videos of up to 15 seconds, up from 10s.
  • More consistent results: stronger adherence to image and video references keeps products, characters, and brand details consistent from shot to shot.
  • Faster drafts, in higher resolution: create drafts at 360p or 720p, then upscale the best creations to 1080p or 4K.
  • More natural speech: You can generate scenes with more fluid, natural-sounding dialogue, clearer lip-sync, and distinct multi-speaker conditioning.
  • Editing in conversation: refine the same clip, such as swapping a product, changing lighting, or changing camera angle, instead of starting over.

Note: Audio references are gated behind allowlisting.

Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is ready for production

Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is production-ready and backed by Google Cloud’s enterprise-grade infrastructure and security, offering Provisioned Throughput. Outputs carry an imperceptible SynthID watermark.

Video creation inside the tools people already use

Design and creative platforms are building Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash directly into their products, so their users can create and edit videos where they already work. Here’s how customers are already using Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash:

“At Artlist, we’re focused on giving creators the control and flexibility to bring their ideas to life. Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash brings exciting capabilities in reference-based generation, video extension, and creative consistency, helping our customers move from experimentation to professional content production at scale.” – Roee Peled, CPTO, Artlist.

Artlist uses Gemini 1.2 Omni Flash to bring creative ideas to life

FLORA uses Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash to create new styles
